newsitem.title: EU: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 21 - SUNDAY, APRIL 27.
newsitem.headline: EC REPORT WEEKLY DIARY FOR MONDAY, APRIL 21 - SUNDAY, APRIL 27.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS ****
LUXEMBOURG - EU agriculture ministers meet (Monday-Tuesday); discussions focus on 1997/1998 price package, olive oil reform, meat inspection negotiations with the United States.

BRUSSELS - African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) Group Council of Ministers meets (Monday-Wednesday); discussions focus on preparations for the ACP summit in Libreville and ministerial meeting in Luxembourg; bananas, sugar, base products, cooperation in development financing.
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro meet Uganda President Yoweri Museveni (Tuesday).
BRUSSELS - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (Wednesday).

BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini-session (Wednesday-Thursday); highlights include a European Commission declaration on the main principles of economic policy and excess deficits, debate on illegal and harmful use of the Internet.
BRUSSELS - Economic and Social Committee holds plenary session (Wednesday-Thursday).
LUXEMBOURG - EU industry ministers meet (Thursday); discussions focus on state aid to shipbuilders and competitiveness of European industry.
LUXEMBOURG - EU-ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific countries) Council meets (Thursday-Friday).
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Innovative research and appropriate health care for the people of Europe" (Thursday-Friday).
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Trafficking in women" (Thursday-Saturday) to produce recommendations for a code of conduct to prevent and combat trafficking in women.
MONDAY, APRIL 21
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Farm Council (and Tuesday). Main discussions focus on 1997/98 farm price package, olive oil reform, meat inspection negotiations with the United States.
Agenda includes:
- Adoption of regulation on beef labelling and registration and labelling of beef meat.
- Commission proposal to the Council on the fixing of farm prices and certain measures for 1997/1998.
- Note to the Council and EP on the olive and olive oil sector.
- Situation of the veal market.
- Preparation for EU's position on forests during the U.N. general assembly in June 1997.
- State of play of negotiations with third countries for the conclusion of veterinary and plant health equivalency accords - Commission report.

- Adoption in Community languages of Council directive modifying directive 92/117/EEC on protection measures against certain zoonoses and zoonotic agents in animals and animal products to prevent against infection and intoxication due to foodstuffs.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Inter-governmental representatives meet (and Tuesday).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission hosts EU-Yemen conference. Speakers include: Yemen Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Planning and Development Abdul-Qader Bagammal. Closing news conference on the outcome of the meeting at 1730/1530 GMT. Venue: Borschette Centre.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Foreign Affairs;
- (1500/1300 GMT) Agriculture;
Economic;
Regional Policy; Development - Chad Prime Minister Djimasta Koibla gives address on the outcome of the elections observation mission at 1515/1315 GMT;
Institutional Affairs;
Fisheries;
Petitions.
BRUSSELS - European Tobacco Industries Grouping and European Food/Catering Workers Union holds joint news conference on "Social dialogue" (1100/0900 GMT). Venue: International Press Centre.

BRUSSELS - African, Caribbean and Pacific (ACP) Group Council of Ministers meets (to Wednesday). Discussions focus on preparations for the November 6-7 ACP summit in Libreville and November 24-25 ACP-EU ministerial meeting in Luxembourg; reports on bananas, sugar, base products, cooperation in development financing. Venue: ACP House, 451 avenue Georges Henri. Contact: ACP House (322) 743 0600.

BRUSSELS - Uganda President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni addresses Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) meeting on "National resistance movement's vision, philosophy and governance of Uganda: experience and the way ahead" (1830/1630 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

LUXEMBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik meets Luxembourg Foreign Minster Jacques Poos; discussions include Slovak EU membership, inter-governmental conference issues, future Luxembourg EU presidency, NATO membership as well as European security issues.

HELSINKI - Economic and Social Committee holds conference on "A Europe for citizens - The advantages of the internal market and cooperation in the Baltic Sea" (0830/0630 GMT). Topics include consequences of central and eastern European integration; single market and the euro - the advantages; cooperation perspectives in the Baltic Sea region. Contact: ECOSOC (322) 546 9207.

MALTA - European Documentation and Research Centre (EDRC) and University of Malta hold "The State of the European Union Conference 1997". Discussions focus on the development of EU policies, especially with regard to the EU citizens' ombudsman; the evolution of cooperation on justice and home affairs in Europe; EU social policy; EU initiatives for employment and growth and the EU's SME policy. Contact: Monica Cauchi, EDRC (356) 32 90 20 01. 181451 DED:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =2 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 2/4 - Tuesday)
TUESDAY, APRIL 22
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0800 GMT).

BRUSSELS - European Commissioner Van Miert address Belgian Federation of Enterprises (FEB) on "The European Commission's view on competition policy and public aids" (1215/1015 GMT). Venue: FEB, 4 rue Ravenstein. Contact: Christine Legrand, FEB (322) 515 0826.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commission President Santer and Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro meet Uganda President Yoweri Museveni.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Bangemann attends "culture in the society" seminar at the EP.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Following EP committees meet:
- (0900/0700 GMT) Agriculture;
Economic;
Regional Policy;
Development;
Institutional Affairs;
Fisheries;
Petitions;
Foreign Affairs - Estonian Foreign Minister Tomas Hendrik Ilves attends at 0915/0715 GMT;
- (1500/1300 GMT) Economic - European Commissioner Papoutsis gives address on "Trade and distribution";
Development;
Institutional Affairs - European Commissioner Oreja gives address on information policy and on the developments of the inter-governmental conference at 1630/1430 GMT.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Trans European Policy Association and the Institut fur Europaeische Politik hold joint seminar on "The EP: towards equality in partnerhip" (0945/0745 GMT). Venue: EP, Eastman room 300.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - The European Women's Lobby holds press reception for the launch of the "Inter-governmental conference petition" (0930/0730 GMT). Venue: EP, Leopold Building press room.
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Slovanian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek meets WEU Secretary General Jose Cutileiro.
BRUSSELS - NATO Military Committee meets.

BRUSSELS - European Institute for Asian Studies holds lunchtime meeting on "The Thai economy in transition" (1230/1030 GMT). Venue: 35 rue des Deux Eglises. Contact: European Institute for Asian Studies (322) 230 8122. 181602 DED:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =3 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 3/4 - Wednesday)
WEDNESDAY, APRIL 23
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Commission holds regular weekly meeting (0900/0700 GMT).
- Adopts 1997-98 economic forecasts for 15 member states, covering inflation, budget deficits, debt levels, GDP.
- Commissioner de Silguy communication on member states' and Community political and economic guidelines.
- Commission President Santer and Commissioner de Silguy communication on external aspects of EMU.
- Commission President Santer and Commissioners Wulf-Mathies and de Silguy communication on the application of conditions for cohesion funds.
- Commissioner Papoutsis communication on a global view of energy policy and actions.
- Commissioner Fischler communication on a Commmission decision on the clearing of accounts of the 1993 agriculture budget, "guarantee" section.
- Commissioners Fischler and de Deus Pinheiro communication on safeguard measures for rice originating from overseas territories.
- Commissioner Brittan communication on future relations with Hong Kong.
- Commissioner Kinnock communication on a proposed directive on airport fees; interconnection of EU transport networks with those of neighbouring countries.
- Commissioner Van Miert proposal to apply merger regulation 4064/89 (Anglo/Lonrho deal); proposal on exemptions under regulations 417/85 and 418/85 for research and specialisation accords.
- Commissioner Monti proposal for an EP and Council decision adopting an action programme to strengthen indirect taxation systems in the internal market.
- Commission President Santer and Commissioner Fischler communication on a single programming document under Objective 5A for Baden-Wuertemberg (1994-1999).
BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP President Jose Maria Gil Robles meets Uganda President Yoweri Museveni at 1245/1045 GMT.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds mini session (and Thursday).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (1500/1300 GMT) - Vote on aid to certain shipyards under restructuring and amending Council regulation on aid to shipbuilding COM(97)132;
- Vote on proposal for decision on the setting up of a temporary committee of inquiry instructed to monitor the action taken on the recommendation made concerning BSE.
- Commission statement on equal opportunities between men and women, followed by questions.
- Commission declaration on the main principles of economic policy and excess deficits, followed by questions.
- (1600/1400 GMT) Joint debate:
- Pradier report on the communication from the Commission on illegal and harmful content on the Internet COM(96)487.

- Torres Marques report on the craft industry and SMEs, keys to growth and employment in Europe - Results of the second European conference on the craft industry and SMEs in Berlin, 26-27 September 1994 - follow-up measures and recommendations to the member states COM(95)502;
- Peijs report on the integrated programme for SMEs and the craft sector (multiannual programme) COM(96)329;
- Garosci report on the coordination of activities in favour of SMEs and the craft sector COM(95)362.
- Tillich report on the adjustment of the financial perspective.
- Le Rachenel report on setting up a harmonised safety regime for fishing vessels of 24 metres in length and over COM(96)255.
- Novo Belenguer report on minimum requirements for vessels bound for or leaving Community ports and carrying dangerous or polluting goods COM(96)455.
- Danesin report on "Towards a new maritime strategy" COM(96)81.
- McCarthy report approving the single programming document for Community structural measures.
- Fernendez Martin report on the development problems of the outermost regions of the Community.
- Joint debate:

- Kellett-Bowman report giving discharge to the Management Board of the European Foundation for the Improvement of Living and Working Conditions (Dublin) in repect of the implementation of its budgets for the 1994 and 1995 financial years.
- Baldarelli report on a specific measure to encourage Italian fishermen to diversify out of certain fishing activities COM(96)682.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - EP Foreign Affairs and External Relations Committees and delegation for Chinese relations hold joint meeting at 1130/0930 GMT. Chinese Hong Kong Affairs Minister Lu Ping attends.
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (and Thursday). European Commissioner Monti gives address.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Green paper on future noise policy COM(96)540.
- Community environmental law COM(96)500.
- Quality of petrol and diesel fuels - measures to be taken against emissions from motor vehicle COM(96)248.
- Problems encountered by SMEs in cross-border business relations, including those relating to technical requirements.
- Simpler legislation for the internal market COM(96)204.
- Green paper on living and working in the information soicety COM(96)389.
- Impact and effectiveness of the single market COM(96)520.
- Seventh annual report on the structural funds COM(96)502.
- First economic and social cohesion report - 1996 COM(96)542.
- Charging of heavy goods vehicles COM(96)331.
- White paper on a strategy for revitalising the Community's railways COM(96)421.
- Minimum level of training for seafarers COM(96)470.
- Registration of persons sailing on board passenger ships COM(96) 574.
- Illustrative nuclear programme for the Community COM(96)339.
- Green paper on energy for the future: renewable sources of energy COM(96)576.
- Cooperation around agreed Community energy objectives COM(96)431.
- Action programme to improve awareness of Community law for the legal profession COM(96)580.
- Control of Pseudomonas solanacearum (Smith) COM(97)15.
- Present situation, problems and potential for developing forestry policy in the EU.
- Measures to improve the production and marketing of honey COM(96)596.
- Support system for producers of certain arable crops COM(97)83.
- The EU and the external dimension of human rights policy.
- Development aid, good governance and the role of the socio-economic interest groups.
- 1997 annual economic report COM(97)27.

BRUSSELS - NATO Military Committee meets with representatives of Partnership for Peace countries - followed by a news conference with Chairman of the Military Committee General Klaus Naumann at 1600/1400 GMT.

BRUSSELS - Circolo Palombella holds seminar on "National interest in European integration" (in Italian) (2030/1830 GMT). European Commissioner Bonino attends. Venue: Hotel Europa. Contact: Luciano Boolchi (322) 649 7275.

BRUSSELS - Union of European Railway Industries (UNIFE) holds conference on "Understanding the logistical needs of industrial customers" (0930/0730 GMT). Venue: Sheraton Airport Hotel. Contact: UNIFE by fax (322) 626 1261.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "The inter-governmental conference - The final phase" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is MEP Elmar Brok. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 3911. 181625 OEC:BC-DIARY-WEEKLY =4 Reuter EC Report Weekly Diary (page 4/4 - Thursday-Sunday)
THURSDAY, APRIL 24
LUXEMBOURG (EXPANDED ITEM) - Industry Council. Main discussions focus on state aid to shipbuilders and competitiveness of European industry.
Provisional agenda includes:
- Shipbuilding:
a) (possibly) Individual cases of state aid;
b) Future of Community policy on state aid in connection with the situation regarding ratifications of the OECD Agreement.
- Competitiveness of the European industry - Report by the Commission.
- State Aid:
- 5th Survey report on state aid by the Commission;
- State of affairs regarding proposals related to art. 94 of the Treaty.
- (possibly) Action programme in the field of the Information Society.
LUXEMBOURG - EU-ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific countries) Council (and Friday).
Agenda includes:
- South Africa: protocol of accession to the convention.
- Trade cooperation:
- Side agreement on white spirits, liqueurs and other spiritous beverages;
- Bananas;
- Modification of the import regime for agricultural products and foodstuffs originating in the ACP states.
- ACP declaration on sugar.
- Ministerial Committee on Commodities report.
- Development Finance Cooperation Committee report.
- Progress report on ratification of the agreement amending the fourth ACP-EC Lome convention and of the protocol of accession.
- Somalia.
- ACP-EC joint assembly.
- Headquarters agreement of the ACP secretariat.
- Data and place of the next meeting.
- Exchange of views on conflict prevention and management and the future of ACP-EU relations.
LISBON (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Monti attends Schengen executive committee meeting (and Friday).
BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds mini session (second of two days).
Provisional agenda includes:
- (until 0900/0700 GMT) Political group meetings.
- (0900/0700 GMT) Ahern report on the agreement for peaceful nuclear cooperation between the European Atomic Energy Community and the U.S.

- Miranda de Lage report on the conclusion of the framework cooperation agreement on preparation for the eventual establishment of a political and economic association between the European Community and its member states on the one part, and the Republic of Chile on the other part COM(96)259.
- Mather report on the strengthening of the business impact assessment system.
- (1100/0900 GMT) Vote on:
- Membership of the Temporary Committee of Inquiry instructed to monitor the action taken on the recommendations made concerning BSE.
- (possibly) Barton reports on the approximation of the laws of the member states on pressure equipment; on masses and certain components and characteristcs of two and three-wheeled motor vehicles.
- Motions for resolutions on the situation in the Middle East.
- Other reports under the cooperation, codecision and assent procedures.
- Motions for resolutions on which the debate is closed.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime seminar on "Lithuania and the EU" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is Ambassador of Lithuania to the EU Jonas Cicinskas. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 3911.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Innovative research and appropriate health care for the people of Europe" (and Friday).

THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Trafficking in women" (to Saturday). The conference aims to produce recommendations for a code of conduct to prevent and combat trafficking in women. It is a follow-up to the fourth world women's conference in Beijing in 1995 and the European conference on trafficking in women held in Vienna in 1996. Discussion topics include the prevention, detection and prosecution of those involved in trafficking in women, and help for the victims. Participants include: European Commissioner Gradin, Austrian Women's Issues Minister Barbara Prammer, Dutch Employment and Social Affairs Minister Ad Melkert, Dutch Justice Minister Winnie Sorgdrager.
FRIDAY, APRIL 25

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - World Savings Banks Institute and European Savings Banks Group hold joint news conference (1100/0900 GMT). Topics discussed are banking and financial sector; main EU political and social key issues in 1996 and 1997; challenges of development in Central and Eastern Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America. Venue: International Press Centre (IPC). Contact: World Savings Banks Institute and European Savings Banks Group joint office (322) 739 1642.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Former Soviet Republics Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia sign the Council of Europe's cultural convention. SATURDAY, APRIL 26 THE HAGUE (NEW ITEM). Closing news conference of the EU Dutch presidency's conference on trafficking in women. (Time not yet announced.)
SUNDAY, APRIL 27
No events scheduled.
